source: RFC 0007 §6.5 (review of 2026-11-21's merges, R3-11: the size of a status; maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-22)
statement: The documents an instance holds, with the revision of each, are its resident record, a record of its own written before its status: when what it holds differs from what its last successful resident write held, and in any case once half the record's life (exactly one hour, no jitter) has passed since then. A resident write that fails does not stop the status write and stays owed: every cycle tries it again. `propagation` reads, at most every five seconds, the resident records of the instances with a live status only, counts those that hold the document and those that installed the revision, and counts as `unknown` every live instance whose resident record is missing or does not decode; no instance is behind only when `installed` equals `holding` and `unknown` is 0.
guards: runtime:ResidentWriteTest#the resident documents are written before the status, and again only when they change
runtime:ResidentWriteTest#an unchanged resident record is written again once half its life has passed
runtime:ResidentWriteTest#a resident write that fails does not stop the status, and is tried again every cycle until it succeeds
cocache:StatusSplitTest#a resident record lives exactly its life after its last write
cocache:StatusSplitTest#a missing or undecodable resident record is unreadable, the undecodable one logged, another's fails the read
control:PropagationTest#a live instance without a resident record is unknown, and a gone one's is not read - CTL-75
control:ClientContractTest#a propagation answer holds exactly the members of its contract file
document:ShadowCodecTest#resident documents read back as written, and a wrong revision is a format error
spi:ShadowValuesTest#the in-memory residents answer what was written within its life and name the rest
